name: dotnet-channels

Guide to `System.Threading.Channels`: thread-safe producer/consumer queues, bounded capacity, backpressure, async enumeration, and shutdown. See [skill:dotnet-background-services], [skill:dotnet-csharp-async-patterns], and [references/detailed-examples.md](references/detailed-examples.md).

A `Channel<T>` separates `ChannelWriter<T>` from `ChannelReader<T>`; synchronization is internal. Create with `Channel.CreateBounded<T>(capacity)` or `Channel.CreateUnbounded<T>()`. Bounded channels cap memory; unbounded channels can exhaust it under load.

For bounded channels, `FullMode` controls overflow: `Wait` applies backpressure; `DropOldest` favors fresh data; `DropNewest` and `DropWrite` discard writes. .NET 7+ supports an `itemDropped` callback for metrics or cleanup.

Producers use `await writer.WriteAsync(item, cancellationToken)` or `writer.TryWrite(item)`. Multiple producers can write concurrently. When production ends, call `Complete()` or `TryComplete()`; `TryComplete()` is idempotent. Pass an exception to `writer.TryComplete(ex)` to propagate failure.

Consumers can drain efficiently:

while (await reader.WaitToReadAsync(cancellationToken))
    while (reader.TryRead(out var item))
        await ProcessAsync(item, cancellationToken);

Alternatively, `reader.ReadAllAsync(cancellationToken)` provides `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` for `await foreach` and streaming. Multiple consumers divide items, with each item read by one consumer. Integrate workers with `BackgroundService` and await their tasks during shutdown.

Set `SingleReader = true` or `SingleWriter = true` only when those concurrency guarantees hold.
